pll1d18c3-d1e3477.summary: Notes that as the Son by birth received not only to be Son but to be at all and to be the substance, so the Spirit by proceeding received not only to be Spirit or Gift but to be and to be substance. He did not receive this by being given, or he would have received being in time.
claims: The Son received being and substance by birth.
The Spirit received being and substance by procession.
The Spirit did not receive his being by being given.

pll1d18c3-d1e3480.summary: Supports this with De Trinitate V: if the Spirit were what he is only by being given, how was he already the substance before there was anyone to give him to? So by proceeding, not by being given, he has to be Gift and to be essence, as the Son by birth has to be Son and essence.
claims: The Spirit was substance before being given.
By procession the Spirit has to be Gift and essence.

pll1d18c3-d1e3500.summary: Cites De Trinitate XV: as generation gives the Son essence without temporal beginning or change of nature, so procession from both gives the Spirit essence without beginning or change.
claims: Generation gives the Son essence eternally and without change.
Procession gives the Spirit essence eternally and without change.

pll1d18c3-d1e3518.summary: Raises a difficulty: if the Son by birth has to be essence and the Spirit by procession, then they are essence by nativity and procession. But elsewhere it is said that the Father is not Father by that by which he is God, and the same for Son and Gift, since these names signify relations, not essence (De Trinitate VII). To be treated more fully later.

pll1d18c3-d1e3538.summary: Answers briefly: the Son is not essence by nativity but only Son, nor the Spirit essence by procession but only Gift; yet each, by being born or proceeding, received to be essence.
claims: The Son is not essence by nativity, but by nativity received essence.
The Spirit is not essence by procession, but by procession received essence.

pll1d18c3-d1e3541.summary: Supports with Hilary, De Trinitate V: God is from God not by defection, extension, or derivation, but by the power of nature the Son subsists into the same nature by nativity, and the Spirit likewise by procession.
claims: God is from God not by derivation but by power of nature.
Son and Spirit subsist in the same nature by nativity and procession.

pll1d18c3-d1e3561.summary: Interprets Hilary: from the Father, the unbegotten power, the Son has the same nature by being born and the Spirit by proceeding. The birth of God must keep the nature from which it came. So 'generation gives essence to the Son' means not that he is essence by his personal property, but that by being born he has the same whole essence that is in the Father, and so too the Spirit by proceeding.
claims: Son and Spirit have the same whole essence as the Father.
They have it by being born and proceeding, not by their personal properties being essence.

pl-l1d18c3.summary: Notes that, as the Son by being born received not only to be Son but to be at all, to be the substance, so the Spirit by proceeding received not only to be Spirit or Gift but to be at all and to be the substance; this he did not receive by being given, or he would have received being in time. With Augustine, procession gives the Spirit essence without temporal beginning or change, as generation gives it to the Son. To the objection that this would make Son and Spirit essence by nativity and procession (whereas relative names do not signify essence), Lombard answers that the Son is not essence by nativity but only Son, and the Spirit not essence by procession but only Gift, yet each by being born or proceeding received to be the essence. With Hilary, the Son subsists by nativity, and the Spirit by procession, from the power of nature into the same nature.
claims: By being born the Son received not only to be Son but to be the divine substance.
By proceeding the Spirit received not only to be Gift but to be the divine substance.
The Spirit did not receive being by being given, which is temporal.
Procession gives the Spirit essence without beginning or change, as generation does the Son.
The Son is not essence by nativity, nor the Spirit by procession; relative names do not signify essence.
Yet each, by nativity or procession, received the whole and same essence that is in the Father.
